learn.hook: Some poems are written just to make you giggle — and that's a serious skill!
points: 'A Funny Man' is a humorous poem about a person who does odd, funny things. Here is our own funny poem.
A humorous poem makes us laugh with silly people, odd actions and surprising rhymes.
Rhythm is the beat of a poem — the pattern of strong and weak sounds you can clap to.
Two lines next to each other that rhyme are called a rhyming couplet (rhyme scheme aabb).
Sound words like 'click-clack' are called onomatopoeia.

example.q: Read: Uncle Bholu wore his shoes on his hands, / And sang to the goats in the sugarcane lands. / He rode on a bullock cart, facing the back, / And laughed till his glasses went click-clack! What is the rhyme scheme, and what makes the poem funny?
steps: hands/lands rhyme → aa; back/clack rhyme → bb
Funny actions: shoes on hands, singing to goats, riding facing backwards
example.answer: The rhyme scheme is aabb; the silly, upside-down actions of Uncle Bholu make it funny.

learn.reallife: Funny rhymes are used in ads, birthday cards and school function skits because they are easy to remember.

games.title: Poem talk
items: Rhythm is the beat of a poem.
You can clap along to a poem's rhythm.
A couplet is a group of four lines.
A couplet is two lines; four lines is a quatrain.
A humorous poem is meant to make us laugh.
In the rhyme scheme aabb, the first and third lines rhyme.
In aabb, lines 1 and 2 rhyme, and lines 3 and 4 rhyme.

quiz.q: 'Uncle Bholu wore his shoes on his hands.' Why is this line funny?
options: Shoes belong on feet, so it is a silly, upside-down action
quiz.explain: Wearing shoes on hands is the opposite of what we expect — that surprise is funny.
quiz.mistake: Looks for a sensible reason instead of noticing the silliness

quiz.q: 'Uncle Bholu wore his shoes on his hands, / And sang to the goats in the sugarcane lands.' Which word rhymes with 'hands'?
quiz.explain: 'Hands' and 'lands' end with the same '-ands' sound.
quiz.mistake: Chooses a word from the poem that does not rhyme

quiz.q: Two lines next to each other that rhyme are called a:
quiz.explain: A couplet is a pair of rhyming lines.

quiz.q: 'He laughed till his glasses went click-clack!' The words 'click-clack' are an example of:
quiz.explain: 'Click-clack' imitates the sound itself — that is onomatopoeia.

quiz.q: What is rhythm in a poem?
options: the beat or pattern of sounds
quiz.explain: Rhythm is the beat you feel when you read a poem aloud.
quiz.mistake: Confuses rhythm with other parts of a poem

quiz.q: The four lines of a poem end with: sun, bed, fun, red. What is the rhyme scheme?
quiz.explain: sun/fun rhyme (a), bed/red rhyme (b), and they alternate: a b a b.
quiz.mistake: Assumes all funny poems are in couplets

quiz.q: A 'humorous' poem is one that is:
quiz.explain: Humorous comes from 'humour', which means fun and laughter.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word humour

quiz.q: 'He rode on a bullock cart, facing the back.' What does 'facing the back' mean?
options: looking towards the rear instead of the front
quiz.explain: He sat turned around, looking where the cart had been — which is funny.

teach.ask: Gappu thinks all poems must be serious. What can make a poem funny?
teach.praise: Ha ha! I'm writing a silly rhyme about a crow in a bow tie!
teach.nudge: What about the actions and the rhymes in a funny poem?

learn.hook: Malayalam is the name of a language — and it reads the same backwards!
points: Homophones sound the same but have different spellings and meanings: sea/see, flour/flower, knight/night.
Alliteration repeats the same first sound in nearby words: 'Pinky's pet parrot picked papayas.'
Tongue twisters use alliteration to make saying them tricky and fun.
A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards: madam, level, noon, Malayalam.
A pun is a joke that plays on two meanings of a word or on words that sound alike.

example.q: Explain the joke: 'Why did the bicycle fall over? Because it was two-tired!'
steps: It sounds just like 'too tired' (very tired).
The joke plays on the two meanings.
example.answer: It is a pun: 'two-tired' (two tyres) sounds like 'too tired'.

learn.reallife: Riddles in children's magazines, jokes on wrappers and ads on hoardings are full of puns and alliteration.

quiz.explain: Flour and flower sound the same but are spelt differently and mean different things.
quiz.mistake: Confuses homophones with synonyms or antonyms

quiz.q: 'Mr Mehta made many mango milkshakes.' This sentence shows:
quiz.explain: Many words start with the same 'm' sound — that is alliteration.
quiz.mistake: Does not notice the repeated first sound

quiz.explain: L-E-V-E-L reads the same from both ends.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word that only begins and ends with the same letter

quiz.q: Choose the right word: 'We bought a kilo of ___ to make rotis.'
quiz.explain: Flour is the powder made from grain; a flower grows on a plant.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the homophones flour and flower

quiz.q: Choose the right word: 'The knight rode through the dark ___.'
quiz.explain: 'Night' means the dark time; 'knight' is a soldier on horseback.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the homophones night and knight

quiz.q: 'Why did the bicycle fall over? Because it was two-tired!' The word 'two-tired' sounds like:
quiz.explain: The pun works because 'two-tired' (two tyres) sounds like 'too tired'.
quiz.mistake: Does not hear the sound-alike words in the joke

quiz.q: Which Indian language's name is a palindrome?
quiz.mistake: Does not check the word letter by letter

quiz.q: Which word is a homophone of 'week'?
quiz.explain: Week (seven days) and weak (not strong) sound the same.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word that looks similar but sounds different

teach.ask: Gappu found 'see' and 'sea' and got confused! Explain homophones to him.
teach.praise: I see! I can see the sea! Homophones are fun!
teach.nudge: Do homophones have the same spelling and meaning, or different?
